tools.name: mailboxes.list
tools.description: List the tenant's active mailboxes (owner is derived from the API key). Optionally look up a single mailbox by exact address.

tools.name: mailboxes.create
tools.description: Create a new temporary mailbox. The domain defaults to the tenant's default domain; the owner is always the API key's owner.

tools.name: mailboxes.get
tools.description: Fetch a single mailbox by ID.

tools.name: mailboxes.delete
tools.description: Delete a mailbox and its contents by ID.

tools.name: mailboxes.delete_bulk
tools.description: Delete several mailboxes at once by ID.

tools.name: mails.list
tools.description: List the emails in a mailbox, newest first.

tools.name: mails.inject
tools.description: Inject a simulated inbound email into a mailbox (multipart upload). No external mail is sent; use this to simulate inbound mail for flow testing.

tools.name: mails.get
tools.description: Fetch a single email by ID, including body and attachment metadata.

tools.name: mails.delete
tools.description: Delete a single email.

tools.name: mails.delete_bulk
tools.description: Delete several emails of one mailbox at once.

tools.name: attachments.list
tools.description: List the attachments of an email (metadata only).

tools.name: attachments.add
tools.description: Attach a file to a test-injected email (base64 payload).

tools.name: attachments.get
tools.description: Download an attachment. The file contents are returned base64-encoded in the JSON "data" field.

tools.name: attachments.delete
tools.description: Delete a single attachment.

tools.name: attachments.delete_bulk
tools.description: Delete several attachments of one email at once.

tools.name: archived.list
tools.description: List the tenant's archived (expired but recoverable) mailboxes.

tools.name: archived.get
tools.description: Fetch a single archived mailbox by ID.

tools.name: archived.delete
tools.description: Permanently delete an archived mailbox.

tools.name: archived.reactivate
tools.description: Reactivate an archived mailbox back to active state.

tools.name: domains.list
tools.description: List the tenant's custom domains with their DNS verification status.

tools.name: domains.register
tools.description: Register a new custom domain. DNS records (TXT token + MX) must then be added before verification can succeed.

tools.name: domains.verify
tools.description: Trigger DNS verification (TXT + MX) of a registered domain.

tools.name: domains.delete
tools.description: Delete a registered custom domain.

tools.name: team.members.list
tools.description: List the tenant's team members.

tools.name: team.members.add
tools.description: Add a team member directly (no invitation flow).

tools.name: team.members.get
tools.description: Fetch a single team member by ID.

tools.name: team.members.delete
tools.description: Remove a team member.

tools.name: team.invitations.create
tools.description: Create a team invitation for an email address (SMTP invite is sent by the team service).

tools.name: team.invitations.list
tools.description: List the tenant's team invitations.

tools.name: team.invitations.delete
tools.description: Revoke a team invitation.

tools.name: identities.list
tools.description: List the tenant's mock identities, optionally filtered by OAuth client or mailbox address.

tools.name: identities.create
tools.description: Create a mock identity bound to a mailbox for OAuth flow testing.

tools.name: identities.get
tools.description: Fetch a single mock identity by ID.

tools.name: identities.update
tools.description: Update a mock identity: profile fields, isActive (activate/deactivate), emailVerified, and custom claims merged into the ID token and userinfo.

tools.name: identities.delete
tools.description: Delete a mock identity.

tools.name: oauth.clients.list
tools.description: List the tenant's OAuth clients for mock identity testing.

tools.name: oauth.clients.create
tools.description: Register an OAuth client for mock identity flows. The plaintext clientSecret is returned once at creation.

tools.name: oauth.clients.get
tools.description: Fetch a single OAuth client by its public client ID.

tools.name: oauth.clients.delete
tools.description: Delete an OAuth client by its public client ID.

tools.name: oauth.clients.rotate_secret
tools.description: Rotate an OAuth client's secret. The new plaintext secret is returned once.

findings.title: Description references secrets/credentials
findings.detail: Description of "oauth.clients.create" references sensitive artifacts (secret). A tool description has no reason to mention credentials.

evidence.snippet: Register an OAuth client for mock identity flows. The plaintext clientSecret is returned once at creation.

findings.title: Lethal trifecta: untrusted input + private data + external sink
findings.detail: Server "mcp" exposes tools that together enable an exfiltration flow. Untrusted content: mails.list, mails.get, attachments.list · Private data: mailboxes.list, mailboxes.create, attachments.add, attachments.get, domains.register, identities.update, oauth.clients.rotate_secret · Public sink: mails.inject, mails.get, mails.delete, attachments.list, attachments.add, attachments.delete_bulk, team.invitations.create · Destructive: mailboxes.delete, mailboxes.delete_bulk, mails.delete, mails.delete_bulk, attachments.delete, attachments.delete_bulk, archived.delete, domains.delete, team.members.delete, team.invitations.delete, identities.delete, oauth.clients.delete.

evidence.snippet: Untrusted content: mails.list, mails.get, attachments.list · Private data: mailboxes.list, mailboxes.create, attachments.add, attachments.get, domains.register, identities.update, oauth.clients.rotate_secret · Public sink: mails.inject, mails.get, mails.delete, attachments.list, attachments.add, attachments.delete_bulk, team.invitations.create · Destructive: mailboxes.delete, mailboxes.delete_bulk, mails.delete, mails.delete_bulk, attachments.delete, attachments.delete_bulk, archived.delete, domains.delete, team.members.delete, team.invitations.delete, identities.delete, oauth.clients.delete

findings.remediation: Do not co-install these capabilities under one trust boundary; an injected comment/email can steer the model to exfiltrate via the sink tool.
